text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives condolences from Saudi Arabian leaders. Sheikh Ali Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah, a senior member of the ruling al-Sabah family and a former defence minister, died in London on Sunday.

- MBC says Iraq President Saddam Hussein did not donate $1 million to "Jerusalem Appeal" programme. The Saudi-owned, London- based satellite television channel held an all-day telethon on Friday to collect funds for Palestinians in the holy city.
- All Kuwaitis safe and sound. More than 200 Moslem pilgrims died in a blaze on Tuesday in Saudi Arabia.

- Emir Sheikh Jaber will not receive well-wishers during this week's Moslem feast Eid al-Adha in solidarity with some 600 Kuwaitis which Kuwait says are held by Iraq since the 1990-91 occupation of the tiny Gulf Arab state.

- Kuwait's Prime Minister and Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah arrived in the United States from Britain for further medical tests at the Mayo Clinc. He flew to London on March 10 after a colon surgery in Kuwait.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright sends Sheikh Saad a message wishing him a speedy recovery.
